maker: (bell sec. only) Paul Hainlein, Nuremberg; slide section from an alto, late 18c. [add to late 18c]
location: D-N, MI 360; acquired 1927 from private collector, from Heinrichau in Silesia.
signature: “MACHT PAVL. [master's mark: in cartouche, cock with large tail, initials "P H"] HAINLEIN . IN . NVRNBERG 1677”.
mouthpiece: Contemporary (x-ray photo in Van der Meer 1979: Abb. 143).
dimensions: bo 10.5, be 104, length of slide section 1270, length of bell sec. 1020, bell sec. entry 14.5.
literature: *Van der Meer 1979: 91, Abb. 143; Van der Meer 1982: 50; Huber 1989: 355.
remarks: Slide sec.: tubular slide stays, lower one solid, not telescopic; ferrules and immoveable slide stay have ring pattern; slide bow has ring mounted on leaf-shaped plate; bumper. Bell sec.: one flat bell stay with tulip, two other flowers, tendrils. Ferrules have ring pattern und ein kranzförmig eingeschlagenes Stabmuster**** . Hinge-plate with leaf motif and stroke pattern adjacent to bell stay. Bell-stay sleeve has seven fields with two different motifs in an intricate stroke design. Ring in bell bow mounted on plate engraved with zigzag pattern.
